subject: dsa
title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
summary: Because the array is sorted, duplicates sit next to each other. A slow write pointer keeps the last unique value; a fast pointer scans for the next new one.
problem: Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place so each value appears once, and return the new length.

steps.caption: It's sorted, so equal values touch. Keep one of each in place and report how many remain.
w holds the last unique value (index 0). r scans ahead for something new.
nums[r]=1 equals nums[w]=1, a duplicate. Leave it and advance r.
nums[r]=2 differs from nums[w]=1, a new value. Bump w and write it there.
2 written at w=1. r keeps scanning.
nums[r]=2 equals nums[w]=2, duplicate again. Skip it.
nums[r]=3 differs, a new value. Bump w and write it.
3 written at w=2. The first 3 cells [1, 2, 3] are the answer; the length is 3.
